title: Emission-slice reconciler: attribute latency & cache responsibility across request coalescing
creator: Marcus Liang
description:
Motivation:
We need a robust way to split end-to-end request latency and per-token compute/billing responsibility when requests are coalesced, prefetched, or satisfied from multiple cache tiers. Current traces surface high-level spans (request -> model -> emit) but do not reliably apportion latency or token-cost to originating requests when KV hits, prefix cache, and batching overlap. This causes noisy cost attribution and makes SLO debugging for tail latency very expensive.

Goals:
1) Emit a reconciled attribution record per emission slice that maps each emitted token (or token span) back to a single origin request or, when shared, a weighted set of request IDs.
2) Capture cache hit provenance (local prefix cache vs shared KV vs model compute) and the delta latency attributable to each tier.
3) Preserve trace continuity: traces should link from request -> reconciler -> serving runtime spans for sampling and root-cause analysis.
4) Make results consumable by billing & dashboards with deterministic, debuggable rules.

Success criteria:
- Instrumentation produced by a canary run matches sampled manual analysis on 95% of cases where one request is originator, and 85% for shared emissions during coalescing bursts.
- Grafana dashboard surfaces per-route token-attribution p50/p95/p99 and cache-responsibility breakdown.
- Upstream billing pipeline can consume reconciled-attribution events without requiring heavy post-processing.

Design summary:
We will introduce an "emission-slice" artifact: a compact event produced at the moment tokens are emitted to clients that includes: slice_id, emitting_span_ids, contributing_request_ids (ordered), contribution_weights, kv_cache_provenance, prefix_cache_hit, batch_window_ms, and latency_breakdown_ms. A downstream reconciler process (stateless consumer in the telemetry pipeline) will convert each slice into attribution lines: for each token-index in the slice, produce attribution to a single request_id when contribution_weights indicate dominance, otherwise emit a weighted attribution tuple. Traces will contain a linking ID to the slice so backtraces are straightforward.

Telemetry schema (fields as strings in this ticket for reference):
- slice_id: stable UUID per emission slice
- emit_ts: epoch ms ISO
- emitting_span_id: tracing span id from runtime
- contributing_request_ids: ordered list string (comma-separated)
- contribution_weights: ordered list string (comma-separated floats)
- token_indexes: concise range encoded, e.g. 1024:1039
- kv_cache_provenance: one of [none, local-prefix, shared-kv, model]
- prefix_cache_hit: true|false
- batch_window_ms: integer
- latency_breakdown_ms: comma-separated list (scheduler, kv_lookup, model_compute, postprocess)
- reconciled_attribution_id: UUID generated by reconciler

Implementation plan:
- Step 1 (runtime hooks): Add emission-slice creation in the runtime at the point tokens are plumbed to the responder. Include minimal fields to avoid blocking hot path: slice_id, emitting_span, contributing_request_ids (short list up to 8), weights (trimmed), kv provenance flag, token index ranges. (ENG PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6429)
- Step 2 (telemetry pipeline): Extend pipeline consumer to accept emission-slice events and implement reconciler that expands slices into per-token attribution events and emits reconciled_attribution_id. Add batching and backpressure awareness to avoid pipeline amplification. (Telemetry PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/387)
- Step 3 (dashboard + billing): Wire reconciled events to Grafana dashboards and to billing ingestion topic (kafka: billing-attribution-v2). Update console to show per-route attribution breakdown. (Grafana board link in comments)
- Step 4 (canary + rollout): Canary on dedicated pool with 2 weeks of traffic at 1% sample, run comparison job to validate against existing sampling heuristics, iterate on weighting heuristics. Gradual ramp to 100% once validation passes.

Rollout considerations:
- Keep emission-slice minimal in hot path: most heavy lifting happens downstream in telemetry consumers.
- Add rate limiting for emission-slice events in high-throughput routes; use sample flags and adaptive sampling based on route QPS.
- Provide a feature flag to opt-out billing consumers until accounting team signs off.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for reconciler weighting logic including edge cases (equal weights, truncated contributor lists, span missing).
- Integration tests that replay recorded hot-pool traces and validate reconciled attribution outcome against golden dataset generated by manual instrumented run.
- Load test ensuring emission-slice creation adds <1% tail latency to p99 at 95th traffic percentile.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Exact weighting function for split tokens during coalescing: simple proportional to contribution_weights vs heuristics favoring earliest request. Decision: start with proportional weights and expose weighting policy as a config in reconciler for fast experiments.
- Storage model for reconciled events: do we keep per-token entries or compressed spans with weights? Compression recommended for long sequences; reconciler will emit span entries with token-range + weights for billing.
- Backwards compat: old billing consumers expect per-request token counts. We will maintain a compatibility exporter that aggregates reconciled events into legacy counts for 6 months.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry pipeline amplification causing cost spike. Mitigation: sample emission-slices and use compression; gate full fan-out behind canary.
- Risk: weight misallocation leading to incorrect billing. Mitigation: hold reconciler behind billing opt-in until we validate with cross-check jobs and customers.
